first_principles_point: Broad technology is the stack that turns digital intent into executed work: compute, storage, networks, power, security, workflow, identity, trust, and customer relationship control.
money_path: customer or enterprise need -> compute/workflow/network/security layer -> product, subscription, usage, license, or hardware sale -> capex/supply/support cost -> margin and cash

first_principles_point: AI creates two different technology stories: one physical, one institutional. One needs power and chips; the other changes who owns the workflow, data, trust, and customer relationship.
money_path: AI demand -> infrastructure spend and workflow spend -> hardware/cloud/software/security providers -> cost structure -> cash or overbuild
company_examples: Microsoft; NVIDIA; Broadcom; ServiceNow; Oracle; data-center suppliers; workflow software firms
proof_needed: AI revenue; capex; utilization; GPU supply; RPO; retention; product margin; customer concentration
safe_use: Safe claim: separate AI infrastructure demand from AI interface/control displacement.

first_principles_point: AI is not weightless. It converts software ambition into demand for chips, servers, networking, storage, cooling, land, power, contractors, and components.
money_path: AI workload -> chips/servers/networking/data center/power -> vendor sales and utility/contractor revenue -> capex/depreciation/supply cost -> cash
company_examples: NVIDIA; Broadcom; Dell; Supermicro; Cisco; Comfort Systems as old-site example; Eaton; utilities
proof_needed: data-center revenue; backlog; orders; supply; inventory; gross margin; customer concentration; capex
safe_use: Safe claim: AI infrastructure is a physical buildout; do not assume every buildout dollar earns attractive return.

first_principles_point: The deeper AI threat is not only labor substitution. It is the transfer of authority from human intermediaries and old software interfaces to platforms that own the AI workflow.
money_path: expert/customer task -> AI interface/platform -> decision, triage, recommendation, support, underwriting, creation -> subscription/usage/productivity economics -> cash
company_examples: Microsoft Copilot; ServiceNow; Salesforce as ecosystem reference; Airbnb old-site support example; Intuit; Adobe
proof_needed: AI product attach; seat expansion; support cost; automation rate; retention; customer outcomes; margin
safe_use: Safe claim: AI can shift relationship control, but proof needs adoption, retention, outcomes, and unit economics.

first_principles_point: When synthetic content and automated decisions get cheaper, verified identity, safe workflow, security, compliance, provenance, and institutional credibility become more valuable.
money_path: uncertainty/fraud/risk -> trusted platform/security/identity/institution -> subscription, verification, security, compliance, or ad premium -> margin/cash
company_examples: Cloudflare; Zscaler; Fortinet; Akamai; Microsoft Security; New York Times as trust reference
proof_needed: security revenue; retention; incidents; RPO; digital ARPU; subscriber retention; enterprise adoption
safe_use: Safe claim: trust is a paid control layer, but it has to be measured through retention, pricing, and risk reduction.

first_principles_point: Compute is capital-intensive. A workload must earn enough revenue to cover accelerators, power, cooling, depreciation, networking, storage, and support.
money_path: workload demand -> cloud/GPU/data center capacity -> usage or subscription revenue -> capex/depreciation/power/cooling -> free cash flow
company_examples: Microsoft Azure; NVIDIA; Oracle Cloud; Amazon/AWS as ecosystem reference; Google Cloud as ecosystem reference
proof_needed: capex; depreciation; utilization; revenue growth; gross margin; operating margin; FCF
safe_use: Safe claim: compute demand is not the same as compute profit.

first_principles_point: AI demand may be concentrated in a few hyperscalers or enterprise buyers, which can make revenue look stronger than the durable customer base really is.
money_path: hyperscaler/large enterprise budget -> vendor order -> revenue/backlog -> bargaining power and inventory risk -> cash quality
company_examples: NVIDIA; Broadcom custom silicon; Supermicro; Dell; Microsoft; Oracle
proof_needed: customer concentration; backlog quality; purchase commitments; inventory; receivables; gross margin
safe_use: Safe claim: concentrated demand can drive growth and risk at the same time.

first_principles_point: Enterprise software is valuable when it becomes the system of action: the place where work is routed, approved, automated, measured, and secured.
money_path: business workflow -> software platform -> subscription/RPO/renewal/expansion -> sales/support/cloud cost -> FCF
company_examples: ServiceNow; Microsoft; Oracle; Salesforce as ecosystem reference; Workday as ecosystem reference
proof_needed: RPO; renewal rate; net retention; large customers; workflow modules; operating margin; FCF
safe_use: Safe claim: workflow control can be durable if renewal and expansion economics prove it.

first_principles_point: Data has to move securely between users, applications, clouds, devices, and models. Network control is a physical and logical bottleneck.
money_path: traffic/security need -> networking/edge/security provider -> product/subscription/support revenue -> equipment/cloud/support cost -> cash
company_examples: Cisco; Cloudflare; Akamai; Zscaler; Fortinet; telecom providers
proof_needed: traffic; subscription revenue; deferred revenue; product orders; attach rate; margin; OCF
safe_use: Safe claim: network and edge control matter when traffic and security needs convert to paid contracts.

first_principles_point: Hardware demand can be real and still cyclical. Customers can overorder, pause refreshes, digest inventory, or shift architecture.
money_path: customer buildout -> hardware order -> shipment/revenue -> inventory and margin cycle -> cash or correction
company_examples: NVIDIA; Dell; Supermicro; Cisco; Broadcom; storage vendors
proof_needed: orders; backlog; inventory; lead times; gross margin; cancellations; customer concentration
safe_use: Safe claim: hardware is essential, but revenue durability depends on cycle and inventory evidence.

first_principles_point: AI features only matter financially if customers pay, renew, expand, or accept higher prices after cost to serve.
money_path: feature launch -> customer adoption -> seat/usage/price expansion -> cloud/support/sales cost -> FCF
company_examples: Microsoft; ServiceNow; Adobe; Intuit; Salesforce ecosystem reference
proof_needed: attach rate; pricing; retention; expansion; RPO; gross margin; sales efficiency; FCF
safe_use: Safe claim: AI feature exposure is not cash proof.
